title: Comparing Length, Capacity and Weight
seo_title: Kindergarten Comparing Length, Capacity and Weight Worksheets (TEKS K.7B)
standard_text: K.7A give an example of a measurable attribute of a given object, including length, capacity, and weight; K.7B compare two objects with a common measurable attribute to see which object has more of/less of the attribute and describe the difference
meta_desc: Free kindergarten measurement worksheets for Texas TEKS K.7A and K.7B: compare length, height, weight and capacity with pictures. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the ends to compare length.
key_sub: On a balance, the heavier side goes down.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Length: line up the ends. The one that sticks out is longer.
  • Weight: on a balance, the heavier side goes down.
  • Capacity: the container that holds more water has more capacity.
  • Say how they are different: “The pencil is longer than the crayon.”

Examples

Example

A pencil and a crayon, lined up

the pencil sticks out

Answer: the pencil is longer

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not lining up the endsStart both at the same place.
Thinking bigger is always heavierA big balloon is light.
Mixing up more and lessLess means a smaller amount.
